domain_overview.domain_summary: The Industrial Component domain focuses on the production and distribution of components used in industrial settings. These components are essential for the operation and control of machinery and systems.
domain_overview.sub_domain_summary: The Electrical Equipment sub-domain includes devices and components that manage and control electrical power and signals. It encompasses a wide range of products, including relays, which are critical for switching and controlling electrical circuits.
domain_overview.functional_purpose: Relays are used to control the flow of electricity in a circuit. They enable the control of a high-power circuit with a low-power signal, providing isolation and protection for sensitive components.
domain_overview.system_boundaries: Relays interact with electrical control systems, power distribution networks, and automation systems. They have physical boundaries defined by their installation environment and logical boundaries defined by their control logic and signal processing capabilities.

primary.name: Relay
primary.description: A device that opens or closes electrical contacts to control the flow of electricity in a circuit.

supporting_infrastructure.name: Socket
supporting_infrastructure.description: A component that provides a connection point for relays, allowing for easy installation and replacement.

control_and_monitoring.name: Control Circuit
control_and_monitoring.description: A circuit that provides the control signals to operate the relay.

safety_and_protection.name: Circuit Breaker
safety_and_protection.description: A safety device that interrupts the flow of electricity in the event of an overload or short circuit.

governance.name: IEC Standards
governance.description: International standards governing the design and performance of electrical equipment, including relays.

terminology.definition: An electrically operated switch used to control a circuit.
terminology.functional_role: Enables control of high-power circuits with low-power signals.

terminology.definition: The voltage required to energize the relay coil.
terminology.functional_role: Determines the control signal required to operate the relay.

terminology.definition: The arrangement of contacts within a relay, such as SPST or DPDT.
terminology.functional_role: Defines the switching capabilities of the relay.

terminology.definition: The maximum current that the relay contacts can carry.
terminology.functional_role: Determines the load capacity of the relay.

terminology.definition: The time it takes for the relay to open or close its contacts.
terminology.functional_role: Affects the response time of the relay in a circuit.

terminology.definition: The maximum voltage that the relay can withstand without breaking down.
terminology.functional_role: Ensures the relay can operate safely under high voltage conditions.

terminology.definition: A relay feature that maintains its state after the control signal is removed.
terminology.functional_role: Allows the relay to remain in a set position without continuous power.

terminology.definition: A certification indicating compliance with safety standards set by Underwriters Laboratories.
terminology.functional_role: Ensures the relay meets safety and performance standards.

terminology.definition: A unique identifier assigned to a relay for inventory and sales purposes.
terminology.functional_role: Facilitates tracking and management of relay products.

terminology.definition: A component that provides a connection point for relays.
terminology.functional_role: Allows for easy installation and replacement of relays.

terminology.definition: A circuit that provides the control signals to operate the relay.
terminology.functional_role: Determines the operation of the relay within a system.

terminology.definition: A safety device that interrupts the flow of electricity in the event of an overload or short circuit.
terminology.functional_role: Protects the relay and connected circuits from damage.

terminology.definition: International standards governing the design and performance of electrical equipment.
terminology.functional_role: Ensures relays meet international safety and performance criteria.

terminology.definition: The range of temperatures within which the relay can operate safely.
terminology.functional_role: Determines the environmental conditions suitable for relay operation.

terminology.definition: The ability of the relay to operate in humid conditions without failure.
terminology.functional_role: Ensures reliable operation in various environmental conditions.

workflows: Step 1: Control circuit sends a signal to the relay coil.
Step 2: Relay coil energizes, causing the contacts to change state.
Step 3: Relay contacts open or close, controlling the flow of electricity in the circuit.
operational_logic.energy_flow: The control circuit provides a low-power signal to the relay coil, which in turn controls a high-power circuit by opening or closing the relay contacts.
failure_conditions: Contact welding due to excessive current.
Mechanical failure of the relay mechanism.
compliance_constraints: Must comply with IEC and UL standards.
Must operate within specified temperature and humidity ranges.

invariants.description: Every relay must have a defined coil voltage.
Every relay must have a contact configuration.
Every relay must comply with UL certification standards.
Relays with latching capability must maintain their state after the control signal is removed.
Every relay must be part of an electrical system.
